transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I hope I’m in the right place, and I really don't want to take up too much of your time. 

Um... I guess I came in because I’ve just been a little overwhelmed lately. It’s probably just a creative burst—I'm an artist, so that happens—but I’ve been taking on... well, a lot of projects. Probably far more than I can realistically manage. I started scheduling all these extra workshops, doing some major improvements around my studio, taking all these new client calls... It felt really good and productive at first, you know? Is it normal to just want to do everything at once when you feel inspired? 

But, um, now the deadlines are starting to pile up, and with the mortgage... it's all just starting to close in on me a little bit. I just wanted to get your thoughts and make sure I'm handling things okay, if that's all right?
Have you been worrying about things more than usual lately?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, not more than anyone else would, right? It's just the normal stress of having a lot on my plate with the studio right now. I wouldn't really call it worrying, exactly... I hope that makes sense? 

I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, but no, I haven't been sitting around feeling anxious or anything like that. Just... trying to keep up with everything I signed up for, if that sounds okay?
Have you been more active or restless than usual lately?

Well, um... I guess you could say I've been a bit more active, yes. But it's a good kind of active, I promise! It's just... I've had this, like, humming current in me from the moment I wake up. 

So I've just been putting that energy to good use, you know? I've been rearranging the studio to make it more efficient, drafting up all those new proposals, emailing clients... just sort of fussing with my supplies and keeping things moving. Sitting quietly has just felt almost impossible lately, to be honest. But it's just because I'm so passionate about my work right now, right? I mean, it's a good thing to be productive, isn't it? I hope I'm not overdoing it or anything...
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I haven't been having any trouble sleeping at all, actually. I've been sleeping just fine. 

I guess I haven't really *needed* as much sleep lately, but that's just because I've been so focused on all the projects, you know? When you're in the zone, you just don't want to stop, right? So I might only be getting a few hours a night, but I wake up feeling completely refreshed and ready to go. It's actually been really helpful for getting things done. That's okay, isn't it? As long as I feel rested?
Have you been having trouble focusing on one task for a long period of time?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? But it's not like I'm losing my mind or anything, I promise. It's just that I have so many good ideas right now, you know? 

Like, I'll sit down to finish a plate for this contract I have, and I really mean to get it done... but then, oh, I don't know, a bird will land at the window, or I'll catch sight of a hardware catalog on my desk, or this half-formed idea for a new workshop will just pop into my head. And suddenly I'm just... pulled completely off course. But it's just because I'm so inspired, right? It's normal for artists to get a little side-tracked when the creative juices are flowing, isn't it? I just want to make sure that doesn't sound too bad...
Have you been feeling unusually happy or euphoric lately?

Oh, um... yes, actually! I've been feeling really wonderful. Most days lately, I've just felt so... buoyant, I suppose you could say. Just completely lit up. It's like my studio and my garden are finally clicking into place after all this time, and it's just such a beautiful feeling. That's a healthy way to feel, right? Being happy with where your life is at? 

I mean... I guess I should admit, maybe I haven't been perfectly pleasant *all* the time. I might have... well, I've snapped a little sharply at a few people recently. But really, it's only when they start questioning my plans, or nagging me about silly things like invoices when I have all this beautiful momentum going. It just breaks my concentration, you know? But anyone would get a little frustrated by that, don't you think? I'm really trying not to be difficult, I promise.
Is this happy, buoyant feeling you've been having present most of the time?

Um... well, I suppose so? I mean, I haven't really been keeping a strict log of every single minute or anything. But yes, generally speaking, it's just been this... lovely, steady undercurrent lately. 

It's not like it's overwhelming or, you know, anything unnatural, I promise. It just feels like a really nice, extended stretch of good days where I'm finally getting to enjoy my life and my work. That's a pretty normal way to feel when things are going well, don't you think? I just want to make sure I'm making sense and not sounding... well, too much. But yes, I'd say it's been with me most of the time recently.
Have you been feeling irritable lately, even on days when you're feeling happy and buoyant?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? Like I mentioned before, I've mostly just been feeling so wonderful, you know? Just really buoyant and lit up most days, like everything with the studio and the garden is finally coming together perfectly. 

But... yes, I suppose I have had moments where I've been a little... irritable, even on those good days. Like I said, I've snapped at people a few times. But it's only when they interrupt me when I'm working, or when they start asking about things like invoices or questioning what I'm doing. It just feels so jarring when I have all this beautiful energy going. It's not that I'm an angry person, I promise! It's just... well, it's normal to get a little short when someone breaks your focus like that, right? I'm not trying to be difficult or mean to anyone, really.
Do you feel like you're capable of accomplishing more than you normally could right now?

Um... well, I suppose you could say that, yes. I mean, I just feel so incredibly inspired right now. It's like my mind is finally clear enough to see the big picture. 

I've been doing these botanical and anatomical illustrations for years, you know? But recently, I started to realize that my work... well, it could really be something special. I started believing that my illustrations could become the visual language that scientific journals have been missing for decades. It just felt so obvious suddenly, and I felt oddly certain that I was the one person who could actually pull it off. 

I know that probably sounds a little grandiose, doesn't it? I don't mean to sound arrogant, I promise! It's just that I finally feel confident in my abilities, and I have all this energy to actually execute my ideas. It's good to believe in your own work, right? I just want to make sure I'm not sounding too... full of myself. But yes, I definitely feel like I can accomplish a lot more than usual right now.
Is this happy, buoyant feeling you've been having constant throughout the day, or are there periods where it subsides?

Um... well, it's pretty constant, I'd say. Most days, like I said, I just feel so unusually buoyant and lit up from the moment I wake up. It's this wonderful, steady feeling that everything with the studio and the garden is finally clicking into place perfectly. 

I wouldn't say it completely subsides, but... well, I suppose there are those brief moments where the mood shifts a little. Like I mentioned before, if someone interrupts me or starts questioning my plans or asking about those silly invoices, I can snap pretty sharply at them. It's not that the happiness goes away, it's just... I get so frustrated when my flow is broken, you know? 

But as soon as they leave me alone, I'm right back to feeling wonderful again. It's mostly just a really positive, constant energy. That makes sense, doesn't it? I hope I'm explaining it right... I just don't want you to think I'm this angry person who's up and down all day, because it really is mostly just this lovely, lit-up feeling.
Have you been consistently needing less sleep over the past few weeks?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I've been sleeping just fine, I think. 

I know sometimes when people get really focused on their work, they stay up all night and don't sleep at all, but I'm definitely not doing that. I might be getting up a tiny bit earlier than usual, just because the morning light is so perfect for my botanical drawings right now, and I'm just so eager to get to my desk. But I'm still sleeping! 

I just haven't felt that... exhausted, heavy feeling that makes you want to sleep all day, you know? I feel rested and ready to go. That's a good thing, right? To wake up feeling refreshed and ready to work? I just want to be clear that I'm taking care of myself and getting rest... I'm not doing anything extreme.
Have you found that you need less sleep than usual to feel rested lately?

Um... I feel like we might have just talked about this a little bit? But, um, to answer your question... no, I wouldn't say I *need* less sleep, exactly. I mean, I'm still sleeping! 

I suppose I might be waking up a little earlier than I used to, maybe just needing a tiny bit less time in bed to feel completely refreshed. But it's not like I'm running on empty or anything. I just wake up feeling so bright and ready for the day, without needing to drag myself out of bed or hit snooze a dozen times. 

It's actually really lovely to wake up feeling so naturally energized. That's perfectly normal when you're excited about your work, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly... I'm definitely not one of those people who stays awake for days on end. I'm taking good care of myself, I promise.
Have you had any days recently where you didn't feel happy and buoyant at all?

Um... no, not that I can think of. Really, it's been... it's been such a lovely stretch of time. 

I mean, I suppose everyone has moments where they aren't jumping for joy every single second, but... no, I haven't had any days where I felt down or flat, if that's what you mean. I've just been so consistently... well, buoyant, like you said. 

It's actually been quite wonderful to feel so steady and positive. I hope that's okay? It's a good thing to feel happy most of the time, isn't it? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm hiding anything, but I really have just been feeling quite wonderful every day.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find less interesting because of your current projects and mood?

Um... let me think. No, I don't believe so. 

I mean, I'm certainly very dedicated to my botanical drawings right now, but it hasn't made me lose interest in anything else. I still love my gardening and reading... all my usual hobbies. If anything, I feel like I just have more enthusiasm for everything across the board. 

I definitely haven't dropped any of my regular activities or stopped caring about the things I normally enjoy. That's a good sign of balance, isn't it? To still be engaged with all your usual interests? I just want to reassure you that I'm not neglecting any part of my life... I'm keeping everything very well-rounded, I think.
Have you made any decisions recently that you might not have made when you're feeling calmer?

Um... well... I suppose maybe just one or two things? But really, I thought I was being quite practical at the time. 

I mean, I did make a few purchases for the studio... just some things I really needed for my botanical drawings. I bought a lovely large-format printer, and some beautiful specialty papers, and... well, some new lighting and a few renovation materials to get the cottage-studio just right. 

I know it sounds like a lot, but I honestly believed the money would just sort itself out once my big breakthrough landed. It all felt so clear and necessary in the moment. I only realized a bit later that I might have... well, put the cottage-studio a tiny bit close to financial trouble. 

But I've stopped buying things now, I promise! I'm being very careful with my budget again. It's perfectly understandable to get a little carried away when you're so inspired by a project, isn't it? I just want you to know I recognize it was a bit much, and I'm being very responsible now.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt similarly energetic, happy, and productive, but it ultimately ended in a crash or a period of feeling down?

Um... no, I really don't think I have. 

I mean, I know there's that whole stereotype of the artist who has these wonderful bursts of energy and then falls into a terrible slump, but... no, I've never experienced a crash like that. Obviously, when I finish a big series of drawings I might be a little tired for a day or two, just from working so hard, but it's never a dark period or anything. I just go right back to my normal routine. 

I've always been quite resilient that way. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I don't have those awful lows? I just wouldn't want you to worry that I'm heading for some sort of fall right now, because I truly do feel very stable and safe. I've always managed to keep my feet on the ground, even when I'm feeling wonderfully inspired.
Do you think your current happy and buoyant feeling would persist if your studio and artistic projects were to suddenly come to a halt?

Oh... gosh, what a thought. Um... well, I really don't think it would change my mood all that much, to be perfectly honest. 

I mean, naturally, I'd be a little disappointed if I had to stop drawing right now, but... I'm sure I would still feel just as cheerful and positive. I'd probably just redirect all this wonderful energy into my garden or... or maybe catch up on my reading. 

I certainly wouldn't just fall apart or lose my good spirits. I've always been a very adaptable person, and I always try to look on the bright side of things. That's the healthiest way to handle a setback, isn't it? To just pivot and keep a positive outlook? I just wouldn't want you to think my happiness is entirely dependent on one thing. I promise you, I'd be absolutely fine.
Have you experienced periods of feeling unusually down or depressed after a period of high energy and productivity like you're experiencing now?

Oh, um... well, I know we just touched on this a moment ago, but... no, I really haven't. 

I mean, I don't get depressed, if that's what you mean. Sometimes, naturally, if I've been working day and night on my botanical prints, I might need a quiet weekend to just sip tea and rest my eyes. But it's never anything dark or... or unusual. Just normal tiredness, which makes perfect sense, doesn't it? 

I always bounce right back. I wouldn't want you to think I have those terrible, gloomy spells that some people get. I've always been quite a cheerful person, really. That's a good thing, right? I just try to stay positive and keep moving forward.
Do you think your current level of happiness and energy is higher than what your friends and family would consider normal for you?

Oh... well, um... I suppose they might say I've been a bit more... spirited lately. 

I mean, most days I've just felt so unusually buoyant and lit up, you know? Like the studio and the garden are finally just... clicking into place perfectly. It's a wonderful feeling, really. But... well, I suppose my sister did mention I seemed a little intense the other day. 

I might have... snapped just a tiny bit sharply when she started questioning my plans for the new greenhouse, or when she brought up some silly invoices. But that's just because I'm so focused on my work right now, and I just didn't want to break my concentration. It's perfectly normal to get a little irritated when you're deeply involved in a project, isn't it? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm being unreasonable or... or difficult with my family. I'm usually very patient, I promise.
Have you experienced episodes like this before, where you felt extremely happy, energetic, and productive?

Oh... well, um... no, I really don't think so. Not quite like this, anyway. 

I mean, I've always been a very positive, upbeat person—you kind of have to be when you're an artist, just to keep the inspiration flowing. But this specific feeling... being this wonderfully productive and energized... it feels a little new to me. 

I certainly haven't had anything I'd call an episode before. I'm usually very steady and grounded, I promise you. I just wouldn't want you to think I'm always going a mile a minute or acting out of the ordinary. It's just a really fantastic creative phase I'm in right now, where everything is just blossoming. That's a perfectly wonderful thing to experience, isn't it? I just hope you don't think it's anything I should be worried about.
